_note: Synopses + first-publication years for the 50 most-mentioned books that lacked a synopsis (Oct 30, 2026). Each already has 3+ mentions or 2+ quoted mentions, so with a synopsis it passes the search quality bar in netlify/seo/quality.js. Year 0 = date too uncertain to state.

books.title: Finnegans Wake
books.author: James Joyce
books.synopsis: Joyce's last novel recasts one night's dream of a Dublin publican and his family as a cycle of all human history, told in a punning language stitched from dozens of tongues.

books.title: Lotus Sutra
books.author: Anonymous
books.synopsis: One of the most influential Mahayana Buddhist scriptures, in which the Buddha teaches that every being can reach enlightenment through a single 'great vehicle'.

books.title: Kubla Khan
books.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
books.synopsis: Coleridge's unfinished vision of Xanadu — a stately pleasure-dome, a sacred river and a damsel with a dulcimer — said to have come to him in an opium dream.

books.title: Orlando Furioso
books.author: Ludovico Ariosto
books.synopsis: Ariosto's sprawling Renaissance romance of Charlemagne's knights at war with the Saracens, whose hero Orlando is driven mad by his love for the princess Angelica.

books.title: Harry Potter
books.author: J. K. Rowling
books.synopsis: Seven novels following a boy wizard through his years at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry and his long struggle against the dark wizard Lord Voldemort.

books.title: Das Kapital
books.author: Karl Marx
books.synopsis: Marx's critique of political economy, analysing how capitalism turns labour into a commodity and extracts surplus value from the people who work.

books.title: Kojiki
books.author: O no Yasumaro
books.synopsis: Japan's oldest surviving chronicle, recounting the creation of the islands, the age of the gods and the reigns of the earliest emperors.

books.title: Lolita
books.author: Vladimir Nabokov
books.synopsis: Humbert Humbert, a European émigré, narrates his obsession with and abuse of twelve-year-old Dolores Haze in an ornate, self-justifying and unreliable confession.

books.title: First Principles
books.author: Herbert Spencer
books.synopsis: The opening volume of Spencer's Synthetic Philosophy, setting out 'the Unknowable' and a law of evolution meant to explain everything from stars to societies.

books.title: The Mysteries of Paris
books.author: Eugène Sue
books.synopsis: Sue's serialised sensation novel, in which the disguised prince Rodolphe moves through the slums and criminal underworld of Paris righting wrongs.

books.title: Eclogues
books.author: Virgil
books.synopsis: Ten pastoral poems in which Virgil's shepherds sing of love and loss against the land seizures and upheavals of Rome's civil wars.

books.title: I Ching
books.author: Anonymous
books.synopsis: The ancient Chinese Book of Changes: a divination text of sixty-four hexagrams whose layered commentaries became a classic of Confucian thought.

books.title: Odes
books.author: Horace
books.synopsis: Horace's books of lyric poems on love, friendship, wine and the shortness of life — the source of 'carpe diem'.

books.title: Cymbeline
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.synopsis: Shakespeare's late romance of a British king's daughter, Imogen, whose faithful love survives exile, a wager on her virtue and a false report of her death.

books.title: All Quiet on the Western Front
books.author: Erich Maria Remarque
books.synopsis: A young German soldier, Paul Bäumer, and his schoolmates are worn down in body and spirit in the trenches of the First World War.

books.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
books.author: George Orwell
books.synopsis: In a totalitarian superstate where Big Brother is always watching, Winston Smith risks everything on a forbidden diary and a secret love affair.

books.title: The Hobbit
books.author: J. R. R. Tolkien
books.synopsis: Bilbo Baggins, a comfort-loving hobbit, is swept off with thirteen dwarves and the wizard Gandalf to win back a treasure guarded by the dragon Smaug.

books.title: Natural History
books.author: Pliny the Elder
books.synopsis: Pliny's vast encyclopedia of the Roman world, ranging from astronomy and geography to animals, plants, medicine, metals and art.

books.title: Tom Brown's School Days
books.author: Thomas Hughes
books.synopsis: Tom Brown's years at Rugby School under Dr Arnold — fights, football, bullies and friendships — in the novel that defined the English school story.

books.title: Critique of Pure Reason
books.author: Immanuel Kant
books.synopsis: Kant's inquiry into what reason can know beyond experience, arguing that space, time and cause are forms the mind brings to the world.

books.title: The Autobiography of Benvenuto Cellini
books.author: Benvenuto Cellini
books.synopsis: The Renaissance goldsmith and sculptor's swaggering account of his own life: commissions, quarrels, escapes from prison and the casting of his Perseus.

books.title: The Principles of Psychology
books.author: Herbert Spencer
books.synopsis: Spencer's attempt to explain the mind in evolutionary terms, treating intelligence as the adjustment of inner relations to outer ones.

books.title: Commentaries on the Gallic War
books.author: Julius Caesar
books.synopsis: Caesar's own terse, third-person account of his campaigns to conquer Gaul between 58 and 50 BC.

books.title: The School for Scandal
books.author: Richard Brinsley Sheridan
books.synopsis: Sheridan's comedy of manners in which a circle of London gossips, two very different brothers and a jealous old husband are exposed behind a screen.

books.title: Ingoldsby Legends
books.author: Richard Harris Barham
books.synopsis: Barham's comic verse tales of ghosts, saints and medieval legend, presented as the papers of one Thomas Ingoldsby.

books.title: Enoch Arden
books.author: Alfred Tennyson
books.synopsis: Tennyson's narrative poem of a fisherman, shipwrecked for years, who comes home to find his wife happily remarried and chooses never to reveal himself.

books.title: Vie de Jesus
books.author: Ernest Renan
books.synopsis: Renan's controversial life of Jesus, which presented him as a remarkable human teacher rather than a divine figure.

books.title: The Poems of Ossian
books.author: James Macpherson
books.synopsis: Macpherson's epics of the Gaelic bard Ossian and the hero Fingal, which he claimed to have translated from ancient sources and which swept Romantic Europe.

books.title: Cato
books.author: Joseph Addison
books.synopsis: Addison's tragedy of Cato the Younger's last stand for the Roman Republic against Julius Caesar, a favourite of the American revolutionaries.

books.title: New Arabian Nights
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.synopsis: Stevenson's linked tales of Prince Florizel of Bohemia, beginning with 'The Suicide Club' and its deadly game of cards in London.

books.title: Henry VI
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.synopsis: Shakespeare's three-part history of Henry VI's troubled reign, from the loss of France to the outbreak of the Wars of the Roses.

books.title: Winnie-the-Pooh
books.author: A. A. Milne
books.synopsis: Milne's stories of Christopher Robin, his bear Pooh and their friends' small adventures in the Hundred Acre Wood.

books.title: Man'yoshu
books.author: Anonymous
books.synopsis: The oldest anthology of Japanese poetry, gathering some 4,500 poems by emperors, courtiers, soldiers and commoners.

books.title: Pensées
books.author: Blaise Pascal
books.synopsis: Pascal's unfinished fragments in defence of the Christian faith, including his famous wager on the existence of God.

books.title: Doctor Faustus
books.author: Christopher Marlowe
books.synopsis: Marlowe's tragedy of a scholar who sells his soul to the devil for twenty-four years of knowledge, pleasure and power.

books.title: The Old Man and the Sea
books.author: Ernest Hemingway
books.synopsis: An ageing Cuban fisherman, Santiago, battles a giant marlin far out in the Gulf Stream, only to lose it to the sharks on the way home.

books.title: The Possessed
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.synopsis: Dostoevsky's novel of a provincial Russian town thrown into chaos by a cell of radical conspirators, also translated as Demons.

books.title: Ode to a Nightingale
books.author: John Keats
books.synopsis: Keats's ode on a nightingale's song, which carries the poet from sorrow and mortality toward a vision of beauty that cannot last.

books.title: The Grapes of Wrath
books.author: John Steinbeck
books.synopsis: Driven off their Oklahoma farm by drought and debt, the Joad family heads west to California in search of work and dignity.

books.title: The Nose
books.author: Nikolai Gogol
books.synopsis: Gogol's absurd tale of a St Petersburg official who wakes to find his nose gone — then spots it about town in the uniform of a higher rank.

books.title: Nansō Satomi Hakkenden
books.author: Takizawa Bakin
books.synopsis: Bakin's epic of eight samurai brothers, each bearing a bead of one virtue, who rally to the Satomi clan — one of the longest novels ever written.

books.title: Death in Venice
books.author: Thomas Mann
books.synopsis: An ageing German writer, Gustav von Aschenbach, travels to Venice and is consumed by longing for a beautiful boy as cholera spreads through the city.

books.title: Our Town
books.author: Thornton Wilder
books.synopsis: Wilder's play about ordinary life, love and death in the small New Hampshire town of Grover's Corners, guided by a Stage Manager.

books.title: The Taming of the Shrew
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.synopsis: Shakespeare's comedy in which the fortune-hunter Petruchio sets out to marry and 'tame' the sharp-tongued Katherina.

books.title: The Princess
books.author: Alfred Tennyson
books.synopsis: Tennyson's long narrative poem of a princess who founds a university for women, and the prince who slips into it in disguise.

books.title: The Ordeal of Richard Feverel
books.author: George Meredith
books.synopsis: Meredith's novel of a father who raises his son by a rigid 'System', and the son whose secret marriage tests it to destruction.

books.title: Progress and Poverty
books.author: Henry George
books.synopsis: George's argument that poverty deepens alongside progress because rising land values are captured privately, and his case for a single tax on land.

books.title: Fables
books.author: Jean de La Fontaine
books.synopsis: La Fontaine's verse fables, retelling Aesop and other sources, in which animals act out the follies and wisdom of humankind.

books.title: Lycidas
books.author: John Milton
books.synopsis: Milton's pastoral elegy for his drowned Cambridge friend Edward King, which turns into an attack on a corrupt clergy.

books.title: The Federalist
books.author: Alexander Hamilton, James Madison, and John Jay
books.synopsis: Eighty-five essays by Hamilton, Madison and Jay urging New Yorkers to ratify the US Constitution, still a key guide to its meaning.
